findings.title: Gain comparison tolerance may be tighter than the finite-difference/solver error
findings.message: The reference gain divides the difference of two Newton-solved node voltages by 2e-5. Any solver convergence residual of about 1e-10 V becomes an error of about 1e-5 V/V in `want`. The assertion requires agreement within an absolute 1e-5 on a gain of roughly 10.9, so solver tolerance alone can consume the whole margin. The test may fail spuriously on other platforms or after small solver changes.
findings.suggestion: Use a relative tolerance derived from the DC solver's convergence tolerance, e.g. `math.Abs(got-want) > 1e-6*math.Abs(want)+solverTol/1e-5`. Alternatively, use a larger perturbation with Richardson extrapolation.
findings.evidence:
positive, c := solveFloatingDC(t, classABDC(1e-5))
	negative, _ := solveFloatingDC(t, classABDC(-1e-5))
	want := (positive.result.Nodes[c.TerminalNet["RL.1"]] - negative.result.Nodes[c.TerminalNet["RL.1"]]) / 2e-5

findings.title: Negative-bias fallback sweep result is not asserted
findings.message: The comment says this case exercises the larger-circuit cold-start fallback that the new `canStepBipolarSources` capacitor branch enables. The test only checks that the sweep does not fail. It does not confirm that the fallback path ran, that the result has the expected shape, or that the gain is finite and sensible. A regression that returns a wrong but non-erroring result would pass unnoticed.
findings.suggestion: Capture the result and assert on it. For example, `res := sweepForTest(t, g, cfg)`, then check `len(res.Points) == 201` and that each gain is finite, ideally comparing against a DC-perturbation reference at that bias.

findings.title: No test guards the live-startup exclusion for capacitor graphs
findings.message: The new capacitor branch gates a startup-path change. The comment says this path must never be used for live startup, i.e. it must return false when `n.dc` is false. No test asserts this, so a later change to how `n.dc` or `n.caps` is set could silently allow source stepping on live transient startup.
findings.suggestion: Add a unit test that builds a transient (non-dc) `mixedNetwork` for a capacitor-containing bipolar graph and asserts that `canStepBipolarSources()` returns false.
